reading.body:
Meta's Altoona campus in Polk County is one of the largest documented data center sites in Iowa, but its operational capacity remains unpublished. The company has invested $2.5 billion in the facility since breaking ground in 2013, operates 400 people in permanent roles, and has built structures certified to LEDS Gold standards. Without a published megawatt figure, its actual scale cannot be assessed against other facilities, though it ranks third among Iowa's three campuses with any disclosed capacity, of which only two have published figures totaling 18 MW statewide.

Meta reports the campus draws 100 percent clean and renewable energy as part of its net-zero operations commitment, and supports a separate project adding 225 MW of new renewable capacity to Iowa's grid. Whether this renewable expansion is sized to match the data center's demand, or represents contributions to state capacity independent of its own consumption, is not specified. The campus's water-positive goal by 2030 indicates current operations consume water at a scale the company considers material enough to target for reversal.

Iowa has 52 mapped data center facilities, but Altoona's unpublished capacity means its role in the state's infrastructure for AI workloads cannot be read from the numbers. Meta's substantial capital commitment and staffing levels suggest a multi-building hyperscale campus, but without disclosed megawatts or rack density, only that the facility exists can be stated with certainty.
